guideword: FORM/USE: 'IF' + PAST PERFECT + 'WOULD HAVE' + '-ED', IMAGINED SITUATION, REGRET|(THIRD CONDITIONAL)
can_do_statement: Can form conditional subordinate clauses with 'if' + past perfect simple and 'would have' + '-ed' in the main clause, to talk about imagined situations in the past, often with regret.
example_raw:
If they had not been there, I would have been very lonely. (Vietnam; B1 THRESHOLD; 2001; Vietnamese; Pass)

If I hadn't gone to these horse-riding lessons, I wouldn't have lost my watch. (Argentina; B1 THRESHOLD; 2000; Polish; Pass)

I realise that if I hadn't agreed with my parents to go to the concert I wouldn't have met Britney Spears. (Spain; B1 THRESHOLD; 2006; Catalan; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'if' with past perfect and 'would have' to talk about imagined pasts.

positives: If they had not been there, I would have been lonely.
If I hadn't gone, I wouldn't have met her.
negatives: If I go there, I will lose my watch.
I would have been happy.

guideword: FORM/USE: 'IF' + PAST SIMPLE + 'COULD', FUTURE, IMAGINED SITUATION
can_do_statement: Can form conditional subordinate clauses with 'if' + past simple, and 'could' in the main clause to talk about an imagined situation, often in the context of suggesting.
example_raw:
If you wanted to do some outdoor activities, we could go fishing or even walking through the green fields. (Egypt; B1 THRESHOLD; 2004; Arabic - Egyptian; Pass)

If you arrived in town the day before, we could arrange accommodation for you at the nearest Hotel. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2001; Italian; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Suggesting hypothetical possibilities for the future.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'if' with past simple and 'could' for suggestions.

positives: If you wanted to do some outdoor activities, we could go fishing.
If you arrived in town the day before, we could arrange accommodation for you.
negatives: If you want to do activities, we can go fishing.
We could go fishing today.

guideword: FORM/USE: 'IF I WERE YOU' + 'WOULD', FUTURE, IMAGINED SITUATION
can_do_statement: Can use 'if I were you' and 'would' in the main clause often in the context of advice or opinion-giving.
example_raw:
Well, if I were you I would go to a small school in the countryside because it's less complicated than going to a large school in a town. (Peru; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

If I were you, I would talk to everybody and tell them when are you free, and spend the summer with both friends and parents. (Spain; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Basque; Pass) 

[deciding between two holiday options] If I were you, I would accept both of them. (Switzerland; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Swiss German; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Giving advice by putting oneself in another's position.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Saying 'if I were you, I would...' to give advice.

positives: If I were you, I would accept both of them.
If I were you, I'd go to work on foot.
negatives: If I was you, I might go to work.
I would accept both of them.

can_do_statement: Can use 'unless' + present simple to talk about an exception, with present and future reference.
example_raw:
I think I am going to pay by cash, unless you accept credit cards. (B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; Pass)

If I were you I'd go to work on foot, unless it's far away from your house. (Libya; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Arabic - Meghreb; Pass)

But unless you do some sports activities you will gain a lot of weight. (Argentina; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Expressing exceptions to a general statement.

positives: I think I am going to pay by cash, unless you accept credit cards.
Unless you do some sports activities you will gain a lot of weight.
negatives: I will pay by cash if you don't accept credit cards.
He did not go to the store.

can_do_statement: Can form ellipted 'if' clauses with 'if' + '-ed' form.
example_raw:
Furthermore I found little rooms where an employee could take a short nap if needed. (Switzerland; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2002; Swiss German; Pass)

Meals are served, if requested, three times a day, unless picnic lunches are needed. (Switzerland; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2003; German; Pass)

Women who want to start a career more often decide to be single or, if married, don't devote much time to the family. (Poland; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 1993; Polish; Pass)

positives: Furthermore I found little rooms where an employee could take a short nap if needed.
Meals are served, if requested, three times a day.
negatives: Meals are served if they are requested.
If I requested it, they would serve it.

can_do_statement: Can use 'If not' as a conditional clause to offer an alternative to refer to a previous direct or indirect 'yes-no' question where the answer might be ‘no’.
example_raw:
Is the Sheraton Hotel ok for you? If not, call me as soon as possible. (Peru; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

Do you work on Sundays? If not, you could do exercise on Sundays. (Mexico; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

I hope it's ok for you. If not, call me on my mobile phone. (Switzerland; B1 THRESHOLD; 2004; Swiss German; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Providing an alternative to a negative condition.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Saying 'If not' to mean 'if the answer is no'.

positives: Is the Sheraton Hotel ok for you? If not, call me as soon as possible.
Do you work on Sundays? If not, you could do exercise on Sundays.
negatives: If he does not work, call me.
I will go if not raining.

can_do_statement: Can use 'If so' as a conditional clause to refer a previous direct or indirect 'yes-no' question where the answer might be ‘yes’. ► Clauses coordinated
example_raw:
Do you think we could have an extra class? If so, I'd like to do it to cover the work I'll miss. (Brazil; B1 THRESHOLD; 2006; Portuguese; Pass)

Is it possible to pay by credit card? If so, which ones do you take? (B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; ; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Saying 'If so' to mean 'if the answer is yes'.

positives: Do you think we could have an extra class? If so, I'd like to do it.
Is it possible to pay by credit card? If so, which ones do you take?
negatives: If it is so, we should go.
I don't know if so many people will come.

guideword: FORM/USE: 'IF' + PAST PERFECT + MODAL VERBS IMAGINED SITUATION, REGRET
can_do_statement: Can form conditional subordinate clauses with if + the past perfect simple and modal verb + 'have' + '-ed' in the main clause, to talk about imagined situations in the past, often with regret.
example_raw:
All this could have been avoided, if the plan had been more flexible. (Poland; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 1993; Polish; Pass)

Several statements in the newspaper could have been avoided, if the writer had taken notice of the income results which were sent along with the other facts from the charity day. (Denmark; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2000; Danish; Pass)

However, I think I could have learned more if more individual tuition had been available. (Poland; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 1993; Polish; Pass)

I wrote this article referring to my own experience in London, hence I might have had a different opinion if I had gone to another city or country. (Italy; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 1999; Italian; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Counterfactual reasoning with various modals in the past.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'could have' or 'might have' with a past perfect 'if' clause.

positives: All this could have been avoided, if the plan had been more flexible.
If I had gone to another city, I might have had a different opinion.
negatives: I could have done it.
If I had time, I might go.

can_do_statement: Can use conditional subordinate clauses with a range of conjunctions ('as long as', 'provided') + present simple or present continuous, with future reference.
example_raw:
As long as it involves children I'd be delighted to work for you during the summer. (Denmark; B2 VANTAGE; 1998; Danish; Pass)

If you're really eager to learn age doesn’t really matter as long as you're willing to learn. (B2 VANTAGE; 2009; Tagalog; Pass)

My client will most certainly ask for compensation covering all losses incurred, unless you manage to find out where the goods are. (Germany; B2 VANTAGE; 2008; German; Pass)

Finally, I am pleased to inform you that we would like to offer a 10% discount provided you reserve office space for eighteen months. (China; B2 VANTAGE; 2002; Chinese; Fail)

Providing we implement the suggested actions I believe we can increase sales within the next six months, overcoming the current situation caused by the international situation. (Portugal; B2 VANTAGE; 2009; Portuguese; Fail)

I would suggest that you might bring a city map in case you lose your way. (Japan; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Japanese; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'as long as' or 'provided' to set conditions.

positives: As long as it involves children I'd be delighted.
We offer a discount provided you reserve space.
negatives: It is as long as a car.
They provided us with food.

can_do_statement: Can form subordinate conditional clauses with 'if you should', in polite, formal contexts.
example_raw:
If you should have any concerns about my choice, please tell me. (Germany; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2008; German; Pass)

If you should have any problems, you can go to an information booth and you will be told which train you have to take to Hassau. (Germany; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 1993; German; Pass)

If you should get lost, don't hesitate to call us. (C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 1993; Swedish; Pass)

If you should have any further questions do not hesitate to contact us. (Switzerland; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2006; German; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'if you should' for formal situations.

positives: If you should have any concerns, please tell me.
If he should call, let me know.
negatives: You should go if you want.
If you want, you should go.

guideword: FORM/USE: INVERTED PAST PERFECT, IMAGINED PAST
can_do_statement: Can use past perfect +  inverted subject, and a modal verb + 'have' + '-ed' in the main clause  to talk about imagined situations in the past.
example_raw:
Had he been more experienced he would have known that these things always happen in this part of the world. (Sweden; C2 MASTERY; 2001; Swedish; Pass)

Had we known this fact we would have organised more activities within school hours. (Switzerland; C2 MASTERY; 2006; French; Pass)

Had we learnt from the mistakes of the past, we would have given up fighting each other a long time ago. (Russia; C2 MASTERY; 1998; Russian; Pass)

Had I known so many people from abroad were coming to visit our stand, I would have studied harder during my private lessons in the past. (Spain; C2 MASTERY; 1998; Spanish - European; Pass)

Had this file fallen into enemy hands, it might have had disastrous effects on the Western world. (Denmark; C2 MASTERY; 1993; Danish; Pass)

Had public transportation been an option I would have chosen that instead of my car. (Denmark; C2 MASTERY; 2010; Danish; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'Had' + subject to mean 'If subject had'.

positives: Had he been more experienced he would have known.
Had I known, I would have studied harder.
negatives: He had been there before.
I would have gone if I had known.

guideword: USE: INVERTED 'SHOULD', FUTURE, POSSIBLE OUTCOME, FORMAL, POLITE
can_do_statement: Can use inverted 'should', + 'would' in the main clause to talk about possible future outcomes, in polite or formal contexts.
example_raw:
Should we win your prize we would like to build a new school close to our production center, for the children of the area. (Switzerland; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2004; German; Pass)

Should you fail to do so, we would have no choice but to take further action. (Poland; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2009; Polish; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'Should' + subject to mean 'If subject should'.

positives: Should we win your prize we would like to build a new school.
Should you fail to do so, we would have no choice.
negatives: We should win your prize.
You should fail to do so.

can_do_statement: Can use 'Were it not for' + noun phrase to introduce conditions in formal contexts. ► past simple
example_raw:
Were it not for my university, I would give up this class immediately. (Russia; B1 THRESHOLD; 2002; Russian; Pass)

Were it not for that kind of toy, children would be able to gain more team-spirit, creativity and self-confidence. (Greece; C2 MASTERY; 2008; Greek; Pass)

In fact, were it not for that reason, Laura would have accepted the comfortable executive chair in a big company. (Spain; C2 MASTERY; 1993; Spanish - European; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'Were it not for' to mean 'If it were not for'.

positives: Were it not for my university, I would give up this class immediately.
In fact, were it not for that reason, Laura would have accepted.
negatives: It was not for me.
They were not for sale.

can_do_statement: Can use 'were' with an inverted subject + 'to' infinitive, to introduce conditions in formal contexts. ► past simple
example_raw:
Were I to win this travel scholarship, the country of my choice would be Japan. (Switzerland; C2 MASTERY; 2001; German; Pass)

Were you to compare people's views on animals to their views on food, you would find many similarities. (Sweden; C2 MASTERY; 1998; Swedish; Pass)

Were someone to decide that he did not want to go to university, he would have to face the consequences of his choice. (Greece; C2 MASTERY; 2009; Greek; Pass)

Were this suggestion to be put into practice, our town's personality would change completely from a small town to a port of call for a large number of visitors. (Greece; C2 MASTERY; 2003; Greek; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'Were' + subject + 'to' to mean 'If subject were to'.

positives: Were I to win this travel scholarship, I would be happy.
Were you to compare people's views, you would find similarities.
negatives: We were to go to the store.
They were to be married.

can_do_statement: Can use conditional subordinate clauses with a range of conjunctions ('so long as', 'on condition that', 'in the event that') with past, present or future reference.|
example_raw:
As a matter of fact, education is free and as a result they can attend whichever university they desire so long as they have the proper qualifications, of course. (Greece; C2 MASTERY; 2005; Greek; Pass)

I was allowed to bring my friends home and go out with them on condition that my parents knew where I was and when I was going to return. (Poland; C2 MASTERY; 1993; Polish; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'so long as' or 'on condition that'.

positives: They can attend whichever university they desire so long as they qualify.
I was allowed to go out on condition that my parents knew.
negatives: It was so long as a trip.
The condition that he has is bad.
